Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input:
G=load()
for p in ['1','2','3','4']:
    i=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    nb={(r,c):i[r][c] for r in range(len(i)) for c in range(len(i[0])) if i[r][c]!=0}
    nbs=set(nb)
    used=set(); R=[]
    keys=list(sorted(nb.items()))
    for (r,c),v in keys:
        if (r,c) in used: continue
        for dr,dc in [(1,1),(1,-1)]:
            s=[(r,c)]; rr,cc=r+dr,c+dc
            while (rr,cc) in nbs and nb[(rr,cc)]==v:
                s.append((rr,cc)); rr+=dr; cc+=dc
            if len(s)>1:
                R.append((s[0],s[-1],v,dr,dc)); used|=set(s)
    singles=[(r,c,v) for v,(r,c) in nb.items() if (r,c) not in used]
    added=[(r,c,o[r][c]) for r in range(len(i)) for c in range(len(i[0])) if o[r][c]!=i[r][c]]
    print(f'--- demo{p}: runs={R}; singles={singles}')
    # characterize: does each run's extension correspond to an anti-diagonal through a cell?
    for s0,s1,v,d,_ in R:
        r0,c0=s0; r1,c1=s1
        line = f"run v={v}, dir=(d,c)={d},{dc}, cells [{r0},{c0}]->[{r1},{c1}]"
        # extension start: which added neighbor of the far end?
        cand=[a for a in added if a[2]==v or a[1] in (r1,c1)]
        print('   ',line,'near-added:',[(a[:3]) for a in sorted(cand)])

def f(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(v for r in g for v in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    seen=set(); out=g[:]
    for cell in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg]:
        if (cell) in seen: continue
        stack=[cell]; run=[]
        while stack:
            r,c=stack.pop()
            if (r,c) in seen or g[r][c]==bg: continue
            seen.add((r,c)); run.append((r,c))
            if r+1<H and c+1<W and g[r+1][c+1]==g[r][c]:
                stack.append((r+1,c+1))
        if len(run)<2: continue
        r,c=run[-1]
        while r+1<H and c+1<W and g[r+1][c+1]==bg:
            out[r+1][c+1]=g[r][c]; r+=1; c+=1
    return out
for n in ['5','6','7']:

import os,re,json,glob
def load():
    G={}
    for root,dirs,files in os.walk(os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR']+'/../../..')):
        if 'sessions' not in str(root) and 'system' not in str(root): continue
        for fn in files:
            if not fn.endswith('.jsonl'): continue
            fp=os.path.join(root,fn)
            try: t=open(fp).read().replace('\\n','\n')
            except Exception: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\)',t):
                k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
                rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
                if all(len(x)==w and all(y.isdigit() for y in x) for x in rows) and k not in G:
                    G[k]=[[int(yy) for yy in x] for x in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
from collections import Counter
# Rule from demo 8: a diagonal line (either dir) is drawn through the shape towards the nearest border edge.
# Actually simpler check: extend each maximal straight same-color diagonal run (any of 4 diag dirs)
# from its far end until grid edge, overwriting background only. Also handle anti-diagonal runs. Verify against demos.
def f(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0]); bg=Counter(v for r in g for v in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    used=set(); out=g[:]
    def cells_of(col):
        return [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]==col and (r,c) not in used]
    for col_ in set(v for r in g for v in r) - {bg}:
        pts=cells_of(col_)
        # find collinear runs in any diag dir with len>=2
        for dr,dc in ((1,1),(1,-1),(-1,1),(-1,-1)):
            for p in sorted(pts,key=lambda q:(q[0],q[1])):
                if (p[0]-dr,p[1]-dc) in pts: continue
                r,c=p; L=1
                while True:
                    nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
                    if (nr,nc) in pts: r,c,nr,nc=nr,nc; L+=1
                    else: break
                if L<2: continue
                mark=[]; npts=set()
                ok=True
                for p2 in sorted(pts,key=lambda q:(q[0],q[1])):
                    # assign to first run covering it? just collect runs later
                    pass
                # mark run cells as used
                cur=[(r+i*dr,c+i*dc) for i in range(L)]; used|=set(cur)
                # extend from end
                rr,cc=r,L*c-... 
                rr,cc=r+(L-1)*dr,c+(L-1)*dc
                for i in range(1,H+W):
                    nr,nc=rr+dr,cc+dc
                    if not(0<=nr<H and 0<=nc<W) or g[nr][nc]!=bg: break
                    out[nr][nc]=col_; rr,cc=nr,nc
    return out
